scope: Read-only production release preparation; no push, deploy, cloud configuration change, browser use or credential-file reads.

repository.workflow_purpose: Documentation check only; no repository deployment workflow found.

latest_github_production_record.verification: Read current GitHub deployments list and this deployment statuses endpoint. This is latest successful GitHub Production record, not an authenticated Vercel alias-to-SHA assertion.

deployment_path.current_blocker: vercel.json git.deploymentEnabled.main=false suppresses the Git integration build for main; pushing unchanged candidate does not provide the intended automatic production release.
deployment_path.preferred: Review and commit main=true in the release candidate, retain dev=true and fra1, then publish to the configured production branch. GitHub history identifies Production releases associated with main SHAs; authenticated project-level productionBranch is not independently verified here.
deployment_path.required_after_push: A new Production deployment for the exact release SHA must finish successfully, then verify www and apex resolve to that deployment and run release smoke. A commit/push alone is not proof of deploy.
deployment_path.alternative: An explicit Vercel Production-target build/promotion is possible only with an authorized Vercel connection. Do not blindly promote an existing dev Preview: build-time public variables and environment-specific API/auth configuration may differ.

rollback.provider_artifact_path: Use the prior successful Production artifact as the rollback target through authenticated Vercel controls; availability/permission of the actual rollback action is not tested by this read-only task.
rollback.git_fallback: If release uses the enabled main Git integration, prepare a new ordinary main commit reverting only the released application changes while keeping main deployment enabled. Distinguish pre-release Git main8a3c257 from the last published runtime235ddff; choose the intended restoration baseline explicitly and preserve intervening developer changes. Do not force-reset main.
rollback.scope: Frontend only. Does not roll back backend, catalog DB migrations, reading activity or user data.
rollback.post_rollback: Verify successful deployment SHA, both aliases, authentication, shelf, Reader and shared/guest access. Old artifact environment remains a separate compatibility check.

environment_requirements.meaning: Production server proxy upstream; API_URL takes precedence. Must target the working backend with catalog v2. The earlier dev incident came from a stale deployment upstream. No actual environment values read.
Public browser auth settings are compiled into the Production build; verify expected project/cookie/auth behavior. Do not reuse a locally built QA artifact with synthetic/loopback settings.
Production canonical/auth redirect URL must match intended production domain, not dev/Preview.
Analytics project and ingestion settings may differ by environment; missing prod telemetry does not prove missing UI actions.
Build upload behavior depends on this secret. Its value was neither read nor recorded; provider rebuilds with Production build environment.

limitations: Authenticated Vercel project settings, production branch, aliases and environment values were not available through the allowed bounded read-only path. No claim that main=true alone guarantees a successful provider build.
Vercel CLI was previously unauthenticated; no login or secret-file exploration attempted in this task.
Public www/apex HTML script fingerprints match each other. The previous deployment URL was not fetched in the four-lookup budget, so this is not an independent exact-SHA alias match.
No rollout, rollback or failure injection executed. Evidence is preparation, not release certification.
